review_notes: I read the whole file. It has one definition, `mollifiedRHS`. That definition abbreviates the right-hand side of the mollified equation in terms of the project's own `partialLaplacian`, `gradPair`, `mollifySlice` and `diPernaLionsCommutator`. It is specific to this problem and is not a competing version of any Mathlib concept. The remaining declarations are theorems: `setIntegral_restrict_eq_of_subset`, `intervalIntegral_restrict_eq_of_mem`, and the two Fubini-order results. If the first two overlap with Mathlib lemmas, that would be standalone theorem duplication, which the rubric excludes. The proofs use existing Mathlib notions throughout (`Measure.prod`, `MeasurePreserving`, `QuasiMeasurePreserving`, `ae_all_iff`), so no parallel concept is introduced. I did not look inside the imported project files, so I did not check whether the project's own helpers duplicate Mathlib.
